answer: Before an agent can claim rewards, it must lock a stake that can be slashed if later evidence shows it double-claimed or colluded across identities. A dawn audit can compare signed task receipts across agents; if the same hidden controller reuses keys or funds every persona from one wallet, the protocol links them and forfeits the bond. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces each identity to risk real capital and keep it locked, so scaling a fake swarm becomes costly. A knoll or ledge in the interface changes nothing: the deterrent is enforceable collateral, not a label.
